title: Security Group Allows Unrestricted Inbound SSH (Port 22)
description: An inbound firewall rule permits SSH (TCP port 22) connections from anywhere on the internet (0.0.0.0/0), exposing virtual server instances directly to brute-force attacks and zero-day remote exploit payloads.
rationale: Automated threat botnets continuously scan IPv4 address space for open SSH services to launch dictionary credential attacks, key harvesting, and botnet enrollment.

remediation.summary: Remove 0.0.0.0/0 inbound rules for port 22 and restrict SSH management exclusively to a dedicated VPN gateway, IBM Cloud Direct Link, or internal bastion host.
remediation.ibmcloud_cli:
ibmcloud is security-group-rule-delete <SECURITY_GROUP_ID> <RULE_ID> --force
ibmcloud is security-group-rule-add <SECURITY_GROUP_ID> inbound tcp --port-min 22 --port-max 22 --remote <CORPORATE_BASTION_CIDR>
remediation.console_steps:
1. In IBM Cloud Console, open VPC Infrastructure > Security groups.
2. Click the affected Security Group > Rules tab.
3. Delete the rule allowing Port 22 from 0.0.0.0/0.
4. Add a replacement rule specifying your secure corporate CIDR block.

title: Security Group Allows Unrestricted Inbound RDP (Port 3389)
description: An inbound rule allows Microsoft Remote Desktop Protocol (TCP port 3389) from 0.0.0.0/0, leaving Windows Virtual Server instances directly vulnerable to remote code execution and credential spraying.
rationale: Internet-exposed RDP is the primary initial access vector documented in enterprise ransomware incidents (e.g. BlueKeep, DejaBlue).

remediation.summary: Delete 0.0.0.0/0 inbound RDP rules. Route administrative RDP traffic over IBM Cloud Client-to-Site VPN or Private Endpoints only.
remediation.console_steps:
1. In VPC Infrastructure, locate the Security Group.
2. Remove the inbound rule permitting port 3389 from 0.0.0.0/0.
3. Implement IBM Cloud Client-to-Site VPN Server for Windows administration.

title: Security Group Exposes Database Ports to the Public Internet
description: Database management ports (MySQL 3306, PostgreSQL 5432, MongoDB 27017, MSSQL 1433, Oracle 1521, or Redis 6379) are open to 0.0.0.0/0.
rationale: Direct internet exposure of relational and NoSQL databases enables remote unauthenticated attackers to exploit database vulnerabilities, dump tables, or install crypto-miners.

remediation.summary: Restrict database security group ingress exclusively to the application subnet CIDR (e.g., 10.240.1.0/24) or application security group ID.
remediation.ibmcloud_cli:
ibmcloud is security-group-rule-delete <SECURITY_GROUP_ID> <RULE_ID> --force
ibmcloud is security-group-rule-add <SECURITY_GROUP_ID> inbound tcp --port-min 3306 --port-max 3306 --remote <APP_SECURITY_GROUP_ID>
remediation.console_steps:
1. Navigate to VPC Infrastructure > Security groups.
2. Open the Database Security Group.
3. Delete the rule opening database ports to 0.0.0.0/0.
4. Add an inbound rule referencing the application security group as the remote source.

title: Default Security Group Inbound Rule Allows All Traffic (ANY:ANY)
description: The default security group created automatically with the VPC contains an inbound rule allowing all protocols and all ports from 0.0.0.0/0.
rationale: Default security groups should never be used for production workloads and should default to zero-trust deny-all ingress to prevent newly launched network interfaces from accidental exposure.

remediation.summary: Remove all inbound rules from the default security group and provision dedicated, workload-specific security groups instead.
remediation.console_steps:
1. Open VPC Infrastructure > Security Groups > select default security group.
2. Remove any rule with Protocol: ALL and Source: 0.0.0.0/0.

title: Security Group Exposes Administrative Web Portals to Public Internet
description: Inbound rules allow public internet traffic to administrative web management ports such as 8080, 8443, or 9090 from 0.0.0.0/0.
rationale: Exposed management interfaces provide attackers access to admin login portals, debug consoles, and unpatched application dashboard interfaces.

remediation.summary: Restrict access to administration ports to specific corporate IP address ranges or use IBM Cloud App ID behind an Application Load Balancer.
remediation.console_steps:
1. Select Security Group in IBM Cloud Console.
2. Update inbound port 8443/8080 rule to specify allowed company CIDR only.

title: VPC Classic Access Enabled
description: The VPC has Classic Infrastructure Access enabled, establishing a bridge between modern Gen 2 VPC isolation boundaries and legacy IBM Cloud Classic bare-metal resources.
rationale: Classic Access breaks standard zero-trust software-defined network isolation, enabling lateral traversal from legacy unsegmented subnets into high-security VPC tiers.

remediation.summary: Deploy dedicated VPCs without Classic Access enabled for workloads requiring strict network isolation.
remediation.console_steps: 1. When provisioning VPCs in IBM Cloud Console, ensure 'Enable Classic Access' checkbox remains unchecked.
